title: OCR Accuracy Benchmark 2026: How Blur and Image Resolution Affect OCR Accuracy

scope.ocr_path: Google Vision TEXT_DETECTION, no language hint, no fallback, no AI cleanup
scope.ground_truth: exact by construction (synthetic render of a known string)
scope.study_type: API-level, synthetic documents; not an end-to-end camera/app benchmark

definitions.empty_failure: successful response with no recognized text, scored CER 1.0
definitions.silent_nonempty_failure: successful response with non-empty text and CER > 0.30
definitions.content_f1: order-tolerant token-multiset F1 for structured documents

headline_findings: Median CER stayed at or below 0.005 through 3.0 px Gaussian blur, rose to 0.157 at 4.0 px and 0.830 at 5.0 px; document failure rate rose from 8.3% to 36.7% to 75.0%.
The resolution knee sits between 18% and 16% of original linear scale: median CER 0.094 to 0.280, failure rate 20.0% [11.8, 31.8] to 46.7% [34.6, 59.1].

Across every condition a user would plausibly submit, 90-100% of failures returned non-empty but materially inaccurate text; empty responses only dominated below 12% scale (51.7% of variants empty at 10%).
Relative scale predicted first-failure more consistently than total pixels (coefficient of variation 0.245 vs 0.598).
At clean baseline, 3 of 3 structured-document failures by strict CER were reading-order differences with content F1 1.000.
Czech median CER exceeded English at all 15 conditions, with the gap concentrated around the degradation knee (blur 4.0: 0.285 vs 0.055; res 16%: 0.540 vs 0.183) and negligible at clean baseline.
not_established: No universal absolute variance-of-Laplacian sharpness threshold (best Youden J 0.505, heavy distribution overlap).
No claim about provider confidence, real photographs, handwriting, non-Latin scripts or cross-provider comparison.
